summary: Phase F testing — Admin role-based tab gating + Governor Manager chapter scoping + Member Card ribbons + Hours HTML5 validation. Backend: 23/24 pytest pass in /app/backend/tests/test_phase_f.py (1 documented failure exposing a real server-side gating gap on /api/email/templates). All data-scoping requirements pass (admin/permissions, admin/stats, hours, reports/members, reports/hours, reports/donations, causes/{id}/donations, transactions). Frontend: All 4 Phase F asks verified end-to-end via Playwright — (1) Governor sees only 4 tabs [dashboard, hours, causes, reports] with chapter-scoped banner; (2) Full admin sees all 13 tabs; (3) Member Card shows email/chapter/member type/joined/membership expires/Ribbons & Achievements section with explicit 'Secure data (passwords, payment methods, transactions) is intentionally hidden.' disclaimer — NO actual transaction/payment data exposed; (4) Hours form has 7 HTML5 required fields, empty submit blocked (invalidCount=7, dialog stays open), valid submit produces toast 'Hours logged — pending admin review' and the entry shows up in the list as PENDING.

minor.endpoint: GET /api/email/templates (and likely all other admin write/read endpoints)
minor.issue: Governor Manager (admin_role=governor_manager) can READ /api/email/templates via direct API call (returns 200) even though the Email tab is hidden in the UI. Server-side enforcement uses require_admin (any admin) instead of require_admin_tab('email'). Same exposure pattern exists for /api/news, /api/pages, /api/chapters, /api/admin/tiers, etc. — only the data-scoping endpoints were hardened in this phase. Recommend switching read/write endpoints for restricted tabs to require_admin_tab(tab_name) for defense in depth.

action_items: (Security hardening) Replace require_admin with require_admin_tab(<tab>) on backend endpoints serving restricted tabs (email/news/pages/chapters/tiers/events/awards/gear/members) so that Governor/Operations/Membership managers cannot bypass UI gating via direct API calls. Currently only /api/admin/permissions, /api/admin/stats, /api/hours, /api/reports/*, /api/causes/{id}/donations, /api/transactions enforce chapter scope.

(Minor) Member Card disclaimer text contains the words 'payment' and 'transactions' (only inside the explanatory hidden-data notice, no actual data leaks). If a stricter substring search by QA is required, consider rewording the disclaimer to e.g. 'Sensitive financial details are intentionally hidden.'
critical_code_review_comments: Server-side admin-role gating is implemented (ADMIN_ROLE_TABS + require_admin_tab) but only used by /api/admin/permissions. All other admin endpoints still use require_admin, so the Governor/Membership/Operations manager roles enforce restrictions only client-side. This is a defense-in-depth gap.
chapter_scope_user_ids returns [] for a Governor with no chapter_id — silently hides everything. Consider raising a 403 with a clear message to prevent confusing empty states.

/api/admin/permissions returns scoped_chapter_id only for governor_manager; for membership_manager/operations_manager the field is None. If those roles are ever scoped in future, the response shape will silently change — consider always returning the field as null for forward-compat (already does this — fine).

Member Card (Admin.jsx L1098-1180) hardcodes 'Secure data ... is intentionally hidden.' — the disclaimer is good UX, but the words 'payment' and 'transaction' appear in plain text, which can confuse a naive substring scan. Cosmetic only.

Hours form (Hours.jsx L46-145): the <form onSubmit> wrapper + required attributes give native HTML5 validation as designed. All 7 user-input fields are required (hours, date, agency, activity, host name, host email, host phone). event_type defaults to 'aop_event' — not user-visible/required. Good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all 4 Phase F frontend asks (governor tab gating, full admin tab gating, Member Card ribbons + no payment data, Hours HTML5 validation + valid submit)

rca of the issue: Single backend finding: Phase F added chapter scoping (chapter_scope_user_ids + is_chapter_scoped) to the data endpoints listed in the spec, but did NOT change require_admin -> require_admin_tab on the endpoints belonging to restricted tabs. Result: Governor Manager's API access is correctly chapter-scoped for hours/reports/transactions/stats/causes-donations, but they can still GET /api/email/templates (and probably /api/chapters, /api/admin/tiers, etc.) because those still use require_admin (any admin) gating. UI tab hiding works correctly — this is purely an API-layer hardening gap. Reproduction: login as governor.tx@clubhaven.app, then `curl -b cookies.txt $BACKEND/api/email/templates` returns 200 with template list. Mitigation: swap require_admin to require_admin_tab("email") (and respective tab names) on the affected endpoints.
